chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: First solo with Paul Ash's band at the Oriental
summary: Paul Ash's stage band at the Oriental Theater, a jazz-friendly outfit with singers like Ruth Etting, gave Norvo his first solo with a band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So anyway we went to the thing and the guy heard us and so he said, well there's an opening with Paul Ash, for the opening show at the Oriental. So, I -- he booked me on it. Now Paul saw me and he okayed the idea that we'd try a solo with him and that's the first time I did it with a band.
With a band.
And it had a good band --
And Paul Ash had a name then?
Oh, yeah, but he had a great band. Yeah, he had people like Art Clayfield, and -- on drums -- good -- good jazzmen in that band.
Yeah.
It was a romping band. I remember we had George Washington, a singer -- George Gibbet, Frankie Banier, Little Watson, all these young people.
Yeah.
And he promoted them. And in the second week they had Ruth Edding.
OH, NO kidding?

Yeah. So I mean it's kind of -- the Public Circle was the whole thing in the Chicago, they were outlying cities, they thought maybe they're going to have maybe -- I don't really know the number, but I know that Benny Murtoff had a theater in the West Side, Benny Kruger, oh different theaters, all around Chicago.
Yes, yes.
And it was just Paul Ash's idea, with the stage band,
Yeah.
So that's when I met Victor, up in -- he worked at the Uptown Theater, up near Northwestern --
Oh, I see.
Now, what I started to do single, well then I started to do vaudeville.
Oh.
And that's where I got the Madison, -- that's an Orpheum Theater up there, Orpheum Time Theater.
Yeah, yeah.
I worked Madison, Oshkosh, maybe Green Bay, all those northern towns.
And that's when you were in Madison that you heard Bunny that first time.
That's right.
Yeah, I see.
